notes: This contract records Umbra's first bounded public timestamped service family in the non-installable IEEE 1516.1-2025 development profile: timestamped Send Interaction for non-regional interactions, with federation-owned queueing for time-constrained recipients, callback-gated delivery before Time Advance Grant, official timestamp/order/retraction callback fields, lower-bound validation from the sender's current or requested time plus lookahead, and pre-delivery Retract. The shared recipient planner selects active ordinary subscriptions only; passive ordinary subscriptions remain declared but do not arrange delivery, although the current timestamped cases do not independently test that selector. A callback-boundary ordinary unsubscribe terminally suppresses an accepted nonconstrained recipient without pretending it received the interaction or later Request Retraction. The separately checked request-retraction contract covers the deliberately bounded legal post-delivery normal interaction path and terminal-designator lifecycle. A focused regression advances the producer to the exact strict Retract boundary while the recipient's interaction remains queued: the callback still arrives, while the returned designator is retained as MessageCanNoLongerBeRetracted after delivery. Connection Lost regressions retain queued payloads through a source-mandated loss cutoff at time 6: two exact-time cases cover a TAR pending at loss or submitted afterward, and a strict-less-than case delivers timestamp 5 before the survivor's grant to 6. A composite asynchronous-delivery case proves the exact time-6 boundary also appears in HLAreportFederateLost; none claims a result for a later timestamp. A separate one-federate regression proves that an eligible-recipient set of zero still yields a valid public designator backed by the lightweight federation ledger; it covers legal Retract and later terminal classification without retaining a typed interaction payload. A default-region companion now proves that a queued timestamped interaction survives a Time Constrained disable/re-enable cycle and still delivers once before its grant with the supplied-empty region marker. An ordinary non-regional companion now covers the same lifecycle boundary without DDM or a source-region realization, proving the joined-federate queue identity survives callback-gated Time Constrained re-enable and that one Receive Interaction callback still precedes the matching grant with the official metadata and terminal retraction classification. A second focused normal-interaction regression proves that Disable Time Regulation temporarily removes Retract authority without terminalizing a pending designator; callback-gated re-enable at unchanged lookahead restores authority for one legal Retract and later terminal classification. A third save/restore regression restores a pre-save live queued interaction and retraction ledger after a post-save Retract made it terminal, then verifies original delivery and legal post-delivery Retract. One bounded ordinary non-regional interaction scenario now drives the same queued payload through Flush Queue Request, Time Advance Request Available, and Next Message Request Available recipients, proving callback-before-grant ordering, FQR actual/optimistic time, and official callback metadata. This contract still does not claim timestamped Update Attribute Values, Delete Object Instance, Send Directed Interaction, Send Interaction With Regions, a complete alternate-advance matrix beyond that ordinary frontier, broader Disable Time Regulation/re-enable boundaries, broader asynchronous-delivery behavior, request-retraction callbacks for other message families, complete terminal save/restore recovery, remote transport, package support, catalog evidence, JUnit evidence, protected review, or conformance.
